ai.title: Preserve user edits
ai.summary: Added instruction to system prompt to preserve user edits. Updates todo.knowledge.md to mark task complete. Covers backend/src/system-prompt.ts and todo.knowledge.md. Addresses risk of overwriting concurrent user changes.

eli5.text: If you were in the middle of editing a file while the assistant was working on something else, your edits are now more likely to be kept intact instead of being accidentally replaced. The change makes the assistant pay attention when you modify a file between its own changes, and treat your version as the one to keep. You'd notice this if you were typing in a file at the same time the assistant was making edits; previously, your work could be overwritten without warning.

ai.title: python-app skeleton added to repo
ai.summary: New python-app directory contains pre-alpha Manicode Python package skeleton. Includes pyproject.toml (v0.1.1, setuptools), src/manicode/__init__.py (placeholder main), README.md, LICENSE, and egg-info. Current functionality only prints 'coming soon' message directing users to npm install. No actual AI coding features implemented.

eli5.text: If you typed the assistant's command in a terminal right now, it would print a short note saying the Python version isn't ready yet and point you back to the npm install. A new, empty Python package folder named 'manicode' was added to the project, containing only placeholder text, a license, and packaging notes so developers can later build the real Python version that mirrors the npm tool. The change is already in the code repository, but no actual coding help happens yet when you run it.

ai.title: Add missing-line-actions patch test fixture
ai.summary: Added `missing-line-actions` test fixture to `backend/src/__tests__/__mock-data__/`. This fixture tests `generatePatch` handling of `checkNpmVersion` client action and `npmVersionStatus` server action additions. Test case added to `backend/src/__tests__/generate-patch.test.ts`.

eli5.text: The team added a new practice problem to the developer training area inside the company's software. It shows a specific situation where a file is expected to change in a particular way, helping developers learn how to handle cases where small code updates need to be identified correctly. No one outside the company will notice this change; it only prepares the software to be built more reliably by people working on it today.

ai.title: Preserve previous files in requestRelevantFiles result
ai.summary: requestRelevantFiles in backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts now captures Object.keys(fileContext.files) as previousFiles and returns uniq([...comprehensiveResult.files, ...previousFiles]). Prevents loss of previously identified relevant files when the comprehensive result omits them. Change is internal to backend request-file logic. Uses uniq to deduplicate the merged file list.

eli5.text: When the system looks through your files to find the ones that matter for a task, it now keeps the files it found earlier instead of throwing them away if the final search skips them. Previously, if a later, broader scan decided to leave some files out, those files disappeared from the results even though they'd already been flagged as relevant. This only affects how the file-finding works behind the scenes and is already live today.

ai.title: Add npm version check and update warning
ai.summary: Implemented client-server version checking via new 'check-npm-version' and 'npm-version-status' WebSocket actions. Client sends local version on connect; backend compares against build-synced package.json and returns status. Outdated clients receive yellow chalk warning with update command. Build script syncs npm-app version to backend package.json.

eli5.text: When you open the app, it now quietly asks the server what the latest version is, and if your copy is outdated, you'll see a yellow warning telling you to update (with the command to do so). The server compares your installed version against the version baked into its build, so the moment a new release is deployed, older copies of your app start nudging you to upgrade.

ai.title: Bump backend and npm-app to 1.0.40
ai.summary: Version bumped from 1.0.39 to 1.0.40 in backend/package.json and npm-app/package.json. Patch release. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The version number for two parts of the system was increased by one small step, from thirty-nine to forty. This does not change how the system behaves or what it can do, so you will not notice any difference whether you are using it today or yesterday. It is a routine housekeeping step that helps the team keep track of which collection of work is which, like labeling a folder after a tidy-up.

ai.title: Pin temperature to 0 in OpenAI API calls
ai.summary: Added explicit `temperature: 0` to `promptOpenAI` and `promptOpenAIWithContinuation` in `backend/src/openai-api.ts`. This ensures deterministic outputs for OpenAI models, matching the implicit default and existing behavior for Claude. Update logged in `todo.knowledge.md`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question, it now gives you the same answer every time you ask it the same question. Previously, there was a small chance it might give a slightly different answer each time. This change locks the assistant's responses to be completely repeatable. You would notice that asking the same thing twice always produces identical output instead of minor variations.

ai.title: Simplify upgrade message in npm-app client
ai.summary: The console warning for outdated versions in `npm-app/src/client.ts` no longer interpolates `packageJson.version`. The message now states 'There's a new version of Manicode!' without the specific installed version number. This change is internal to the CLI client's update notification logic.

eli5.text: When you run this tool, it occasionally warns you that a newer version exists. That warning used to show the exact version currently installed on your machine alongside the newest available version. Now the warning simply says 'There's a new version of Manicode!' without listing the specific installed version number. This is an internal adjustment to the upgrade notification text only; the tool still detects outdated versions and still suggests you run the same update command. The change is live today whenever you trigger a version check.

ai.title: Disable ensureDirectoryExists in ChatStorage constructor
ai.summary: The `ensureDirectoryExists` call is commented out in the `ChatStorage` constructor within `npm-app/src/chat-storage.ts`. This change prevents the automatic creation of empty chat directories during initialization. The modification is internal to the storage logic and does not affect user-facing features or model availability.

eli5.text: When the app starts up, it used to automatically create a new folder to store your chat history. Now it skips that step during startup and only sets things up when you actually need to save something. The behind-the-scenes change affects how the app prepares itself to store conversations; you won't see empty folders being made ahead of time.

ai.title: Apply file changes immediately per tool call
ai.summary: System prompt no longer defers file edits until response end; changes apply immediately per tool call. `ChatStorage.saveFilesChanged` merges new file states into current version before `applyChanges` runs in `client.ts` and `cli.ts`. Covers npm-app client, CLI, and chat storage. Ensures context reflects latest disk state during multi-step tool sequences.

eli5.text: When the assistant writes or edits your files, those changes now take effect immediately with each step, instead of all happening at once at the very end. This means the assistant always sees the most up-to-date version of your files as it works through multi-step tasks, reducing confusion or conflicts. The change affects the tool that handles file saving behind the scenes and is already live today.

ai.title: Bump backend and manicode to 1.0.41
ai.summary: Version bumped 1.0.40 to 1.0.41. Applies to backend and npm-app (manicode) package.json files. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The two pieces of software that power the backend and the coding assistant were quietly moved forward to the next small version number. Nothing you can see changes when you open the app today, because the only edits were a pair of version labels swapped from forty to forty-one. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping to keep a clean starting point for future changes, like rolling the odometer without touching the engine.

ai.title: Added authentication and billing knowledge plan
ai.summary: Added authentication_and_billing.knowledge.md detailing planned auth, PostgreSQL, OAuth, Stripe, and usage limits for Manicode. Updated todo.knowledge.md to mark completed items (Dawson case, marker token, out-of-date message) and add new notes on file diff context and update_file_context behavior.

eli5.text: The team added a written plan that describes upcoming features for logging in and paying for Manicode: a username/password login for the console, a PostgreSQL database to store accounts, Google and GitHub login buttons, referral links, Stripe payments, and per-user usage limits. The change is a planning document, so nothing new works today and users will not notice anything different. Anyone tracking the project's roadmap can now read the full set of intended authentication and billing steps in one place, rather than scattered across notes. The project's running checklist was also updated to mark a few finished items and add a couple of new behind-the-scenes notes.
